findings.oracle: Real HexEditorBridge with no document opened; bridge.document is None + bridge.state.binary_loaded is False + bridge.state.target_path is None asserted before the call, RuntimeError matching 'no document open' asserted on call, and same three state fields re-asserted after - proving the guard fired for the correct reason and left no partial state.

Real BuiltinFunctions backed by DataReader.from_bytes(bytes(4)); pytest.raises(HexPatRuntimeError, match=r"cannot parse 'not-an-int' as base-10 integer") asserts the exact error text, and isinstance(exc_info.value.__cause__, ValueError) proves the original parse exception was chained rather than a different code path firing.

Live OpenAI connect (real /models round-trip); after disconnect: provider.client is None asserts client teardown beyond a flag toggle, and a subsequent list_models() call asserts ProviderError with exact 'Not connected to OpenAI API' message - proving the not-connected guard sees a genuinely torn-down client.

Real structlog BoundLogger with isolated stdlib handler; after all six non-object payloads (int, list, str, null, bool x2) each return None, _read_events(stream) == [] proves silence; a control call with '{not json' on the same logger then asserts exactly one warning event, making the empty-events assertion non-vacuous.
